title: Cajun Haloumi Schnitzels
subtitle: with Braised Veggies and Spring Onion
description: Whether you're full-time vego or part-time only, our varied range of vegetarian dishes really hits the spot. Bursting with veggies, dairy, legumes, grains and nuts, they're packed with flavour, they’ll fill you up and they're totally mouth-watering too!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Halve the carrot lengthwise and thinly slice. Thinly slice the spring onion. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. Cut the haloumi in half horizontally to make 2 thin slices.

Crumb haloumi: Whisk 1 egg in a shallow bowl. Put 1 tbs plain flour and 1½ tsp Cajun seasoning (see Make it milder) in a separate shallow bowl, season with salt and pepper and stir to combine. Put the breadcrumbs in a third shallow bowl. Dust the haloumi in the flour mixture, shake off the excess, then dip in the egg and coat in the breadcrumbs.

Pan-fry schnitzels: Heat 2 tbs olive oil in a medium frypan over medium heat. Cook the haloumi schnitzels for 2-3 mins each side until golden and cooked through. Remove from the pan and drain on paper towel. Season with salt and pepper.

Braise veggies: Meanwhile, heat 2 tsp olive oil in a medium deep frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the carrot, garlic and half the spring onion, stirring, for 3 mins or until softened. Add the peas and 185ml (¾ cup) hot water and season with salt and pepper. Bring to the boil, then reduce heat to medium and cook for 5-8 mins until liquid is mostly absorbed. Remove pan from the heat.

Serve up: Combine ½ tsp Cajun seasoning, 2 tbs mayonnaise and 1 tbs warm water in a bowl. Divide the schnitzels and veggies among plates and drizzle the schnitzels with the Cajun mayonnaise. Scatter over the remaining spring onion, season with salt and pepper and enjoy!

Make it milder: you prefer, leave the skin on and simply dust the fish with the flour and seasoning mixture before cooking (skip coating in the egg and breadcrumbs). ~ Our Cajun seasoning has a chilli kick. If you aren't a fan of too much heat, leave it out or add less to your taste.
